This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- from the respondents, for the grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 15-04-2024, the petitioner was going towards Bengaluru city from his village Rayappanahalli by riding the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-03-ES-6444 along with his sister Nalini P., and his relative Madhushree M., as pillion riders, slowly,
cautiously, on the correct side of Shidlagatta- Bengaluru road.

On the way at about 8.40 a.m., infront of Primary School, Ramalingapura Village, Shidlagatta Taluk,
Chikkaballapura District, the driver of the car bearing Reg. No.KA-40-A-9477 came from Shidlagatta side, with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, came towards wrong side of the road and dashed against the motorcycle of the petitioner.
Due to the said impact, all the occupants of the motorcycle knocked down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to Government Hospital, Chikkaballapura, wherein he took first aid treatment and then he was shifted to Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he took treatment as an in-patient.
Earlier to the accident, he was working as an agriculturist and was earning a sum of Rs.30,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
The Dibburahalli Police have registered the case against the driver of the said car for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 337 of I.P.C.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- with interest.
3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondents No.1 and 2 have appeared through their counsel and filed their separate written statements.
4. The respondent No.1 in his written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.

He has contended that, the driver of his car bearing No.KA-40-A- 9477 was driving the same on the left side of Shidlaghatta road, slowly, carefully and cautiously, by observing all traffic rules and regulations, as there was no traffic on the said road.

When the said car reached at the alleged place of accident, the petitioner who was not wearing helmet, not holding valid driving licence, rode the motorcycle bearing No.KA-03-ES-6444, along with two pillion riders, at high speed, in a rash and negligent and due to high speed he lost control over his motorcycle and dashed against the car Mahesh P vs Srikanth H N on 3 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/7177139/
2 bearing No.KA-40-A-9477 and fell down and sustained simple injuries. The said accident has occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the petitioner himself and the driver of car bearing No.KA-40-A-9477 was not at all responsible for the alleged accident.

Further it is contended that, he is the registered certificate owner of the car bearing No.KA-40-A-9477 and all the records pertaining to the said car are standing in his name and the said car was insured with the respondent No.2 i.e. IFFCO-TOKIO General Insurance Co. Ltd., under the policy No.13522742 and same was valid from 12-06-2023 to 11-06-2024 and as on the alleged date of accident the insurance policy was valid and in force and the driver of his car was holding valid and effective driving licence to drive the said car.
If at all, the petitioner is entitled for any compensation, the same has to be paid or indemnified by the respondent No.2.
Further, he has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries sustained, medical expenses incurred and treatment taken by him.
The compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
For the above denials and contentions, he has prayed to dismiss the petition.
5. Whereas, the respondent No.2 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.

It has admitted the issuance of insurance policy in respect of car bearing Reg.
No.KA-40-A-9477 in favour of respondent No.1 and its validity as on the date of accident.
It seeks protection under Section 56, 66, 147, 149(2) and 150 of Motor Vehicles Act.
Further it is contended that, the petition is bad for non- compliance of provision under Section 134(c) and 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act.
Further, it has sought permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.1, as per Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act.

Further it is contended that, the car bearing No.KA-40-A-9477 was not at all involved in the alleged accident, the petitioner himself was solely responsible for the alleged accident, the said car is falsely implicated by the petitioner in collusion with the owner of the vehicle, hospital authorities and police, to get compensation from this respondent.
Further it is contended that, the petitioner was not wearing helmet as on the date of accident.
As such, he has violated Section 129 of the Motor Vehicles Act.

Further it is contended that, as per the police documents, three persons were traveling on a two-wheeler, in the event of three persons traveling on a motorcycle each one of them has contributed their negligence in causing the accident.
Further it is contended that, the driver of the car was not holding valid and effective driving licence to drive the particular class of vehicle as on the date of accident.
The respondent No.1 knowing fully well that the driver did not have valid driving licence as on the date of accident has entrusted his vehicle to the said driver.
The jurisdictional police after investigation filed charge-sheet against the insured vehicle driver under Section 279 and 338 of I.P.C. and 181 of Motor Vehicles Act.
Thereby, the owner of the vehicle has committed breach of terms and conditions of the policy.
Further it is contended that, the car bearing No.KA-40-A-9477 was not holding valid fitness certificate and permit as on the date of accident.
It has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries sustained, medical expenses incurred and treatment taken by him.
Further it is contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
For the above denials and contentions, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

12. On meticulously going through the above police documents marked as Ex.P.1 to 6 and 8,
prima-facia it reveals that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg. No.KA-40-A-9477 and dashing the same to the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-03-ES-6444 of the petitioner, from opposite direction.
Due to said impact the petitioner has fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

The investigation officer in his final report, marked as Ex.P.6, has clearly stated that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg.
No.KA- 40-A-9477.
13.

At the outset, it is pertinent to note that, in the present case, the date, time and place of accident,
involvement of car bearing Reg. No.KA-40-A-9477 in the said accident, issuance of insurance policy by the respondent No.2 in respect of said vehicle and its validity as on the date of accident, are not in dispute.

But, the respondent No.1 & 2 have specifically denied the above averred facts and circumstances of the accident and taken specific defence that, the alleged accident has taken place solely due to the rash and negligent riding of the petitioner/rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-03- ES-6444 and there was no negligence on the part of the driver of car bearing Reg.
No.KA-40-A-9477.

Further it is contended that, the petitioner in collusion with the police authorities and respondent No.1 has got registered a false case against the driver of said car, to get wrongful gain from the respondents.
But, the respondents have failed to establish the said contentions.

They have neither adduced any evidence, nor they have produced any document to show that, the said accident has solely taken place due to the rash and negligent riding of the petitioner/rider of motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-03-ES-6444 himself and there was no negligence on the part of the driver of offending car bearing Reg. No.KA-40-A-9477.

On the other hand, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg.
No.KA-40-A-9477 and dashing the same to the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-03- ES-6444 of the petitioner, from opposite direction

. Though, the learned counsel for respondents No.1 and 2 have cross- examined P.W.1 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence or which goes to show that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the petitioner/rider of motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-03-ES- 6444 or there was any contributory negligence on his part in the cause of accident.
14. But, it is pertinent to note that, admittedly, at the time of accident the P.W.1/ rider of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-03-ES-6444 was riding the same along with two pillion riders.

There are every chances that, due to three persons traveling on a motorcycle, which is meant for two persons,
there would be congestion to the rider of said motorcycle and he might have lost control resulting in the accident.
Hence, this Court is of the opinion that, the petitioner/rider of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-03-ES- 6444 is also liable for contributory negligence in the cause of accident.

But, as there Mahesh P vs Srikanth H N on 3 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/7177139/

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report of the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle, rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.

17. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011) 11 SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."

20. Issue No.2:

While answering above issue this Court has come to conclusion that, the accident in question has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg.
No.KA-40-A-9477 and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.
As per the medical records placed on record by the petitioner, he has sustained fracture mid shaft of right femur and degloving injury of right forearm.
Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.

The damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e. pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment, attendants, transport, actual loss of earning, future loss of earning etc., and non-pecuniary damages, such as mental and physical shock,
loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life, loss of prospects of marriage etc.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
i) Towards loss of future income:
In order to determine the compensation towards loss of future income, the age, monthly income and disability of the petitioner are to be determined.
To prove his age, the petitioner has produced the notarised copy of his Aadhar card, which is marked as Ex.P.7.
As per Ex.P.7, the date of birth of the petitioner is 12-07-2000.
The accident has taken place on 15-04-2024 at about 8.40 a.m.
This clearly goes to show that, the age of the petitioner as on the date of accident was 24 years.

Further, the P.W.2, who is the doctor who has examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessment of disability, has clearly deposed in his examination-in-chief affidavit that, on clinical examination he found that, the petitioner has suffered fracture mid shaft of right femur and degloving injury of right forearm and for the said injuries the petitioner has undergone surgeries.

Further he has deposed that, on clinical and radiological examination of injuries suffered by the petitioner he found that, the petitioner has suffered permanent physical disability of 50.07% to right lower limb, 15.79% to right upper limb and 19% to the whole body.

Further, the Ex.P.8 wound certificate, Ex.P.9 to 11 and 15 discharge summaries (total 4), Ex.P.14 x-ray films (total 8), Ex.P.17 disability assessment chart, Ex.P.18 x-rays (total 2) and Ex.P.21 case-sheets (total Mahesh P vs Srikanth H N on 3 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/7177139/

Therefore, in such circumstances and taking into consideration the age of the petitioner, injuries sustained, avocation of the petitioner, duration of treatment and oral and documentary evidence on record, this Court is of the opinion that, considering the disability of 15% to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified.
Hence, in the instant case the disability of 15% to the whole body of the petitioner is considered.
a) The petitioner has deposed in his evidence that, before accident he was working as an agriculturist and was earning a sum of Rs.30,000/- per month.
Further, he has deposed that, due to grievous injuries suffered in the said accident he is unable to do his work.
The respondents have specifically denied the same.
In such circumstances, the burden was on the petitioner to prove his avocation and income.
But, the petitioner has failed to establish the same through cogent and corroborative evidence.
He has not produced any document to show that, before accident he was working as an agriculturist and was earning a sum of Rs.30,000/- per month.
Therefore, in such circumstances, there is no other option before this Court, except to consider the notional income as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
The accident has taken place in the year 2024.

Hence, the notional income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.16,500/- per month and the annual income of the petitioner as Rs.1,98,000/-.
b)

As per the ratio laid down in the case of Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in 2009 ACJ 1298, the appropriate multiplier for a person whose is aged about 24 years is 18.

opennyai_summary.facts:
This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- from the respondents, for the grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.
Earlier to the accident, he was working as an agriculturist and was earning a sum of Rs.30,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
The Dibburahalli Police have registered the case against the driver of the said car for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 337 of I.P.C.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
If at all, the petitioner is entitled for any compensation, the same has to be paid or indemnified by the respondent No.2.
opennyai_summary.arguments:

The jurisdictional police after investigation filed charge-sheet against the insured vehicle driver under Section 279 and 338 of I.P.C. and 181 of Motor Vehicles Act.
